children: Egypt’s Pharco Pharmaceuticals plans to start operations at a new factory it is building in Saudi Arabia’s Medina by mid-2027, Chairman Sherine Helmy said on the sidelines of an event in Cairo on Tuesday.

Pharco traces its origins to 1957, when it began as a pharmacy, before moving into pharmaceutical manufacturing in the 1980s and starting production in 1987. The company currently develops, manufactures, and markets medicines, with about 450 products. It has offices in countries including Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Yemen, Libya and Romania, and exports its products to more than 50 countries, according to its website.

The group already holds a minority stake in a pharmaceutical factory in Saudi Arabia and is now building a new facility with an investment of 2.5 billion Egyptian pounds ($49 million) as part of its expansion plans.
“We are building a factory in Medina. It will be ready and start operations in mid-2027,” Helmy said, adding that the number of products to be manufactured at the facility has yet to be determined.
Asked about plans to expand into other markets, Helmy said the group is currently studying opportunities in Africa and is targeting two markets, though it has yet to decide which countries.
“We visited Angola, Burkina Faso and Ghana, as well as Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya. We haven’t yet settled on the two countries,” he said.
The group also plans to invest about 1 billion Egyptian pounds in its factories in Egypt through the end of 2027 to develop and open new departments and improve the efficiency of production lines.

title: Egypt’s Pharco Pharmaceuticals targets mid-2027 start for Saudi plant
